title: Eddie and Sugarlou and Troy Floyd's record labels
summary: Albert worked with Eddie and Sugarlou in Longview with Troy's band; they discuss Vocalion and OKeh labels and Troy's blues recordings.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Oh, I worked with them in the little town of Longview, Texas. How long were they with them? Oh, we played maybe a week or two at a time. And that's when I was with Troy's band. And we made those, after we tried his band I think, I might have made something with Eddie and Sugarloo on one of the recordings, but I can't find it.

I might have it at school. Maybe so I'll be fine if I'd like to hear it. I think they made the KWK blues or something like that. Yeah. But, and I, you know, I can't remember offhand, but I had the old vocalion and then it got broken.
Well, the old vocalions, that was the first one. And then it went into the OKEH, which just said OKRUNS. Well, because that's the one that Troy made the Chattanoid blues on and also Dreamland.
